newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Inbound cargo security improves at Dar es Salaam.
newsitem.headline: Inbound cargo security improves at Dar es Salaam.

text.p: Security of inbound cargo during handling at Tanzania's international airport in Dar es Salaam has improved significantly during the last few months, a senior government official said.

Salum Msoma, principal secretary at the Ministry of Communications and Transport, told Reuters the government had implemented tighter control on personnel movements at the airport after a series of complaints from freight firms about "disappearing cargo" earlier in the year.
He was speaking during a workshop on privatisation.
Local freight forwarders present at the workshop agreed that the newly imposed strict identification checks were working efficiently, making it more difficult for corruption to take place.

"The security has improved greatly at the cargo terminal. Now you won't be allowed into the cargo terminal without identification from your company," said Freight Forwarders Association of Tanzania (FFAT) president said Merad Mutungi.
"The official state-owned airport cargo handling company TAHACO also insists that you have a letter from the importer of the cargo authorising you to clear it," said Mutungi.
He added that since the new rules were reinforced last month the association had received no new complaints of cargo disappearing from the terminal.
He said he wanted to tighten control at the terminal even further through the use of identity cards issued by the association but this had not been finalised.
In a related development Salum Msoma said the government recently had purchased for more than $3 million worth of new handling equipment for the airport to replace outdated equipment.

Asked whether the government was planning to privatise the airport, Msoma replied the government " wanted to commercialise the airport" and was discussing how to partly privatise the utility, but he could not disclose any more details at this time.
